pairs.difference: A: the telescope tube is one even lacquer with a clean long highlight, the gold rings match it, and gloss (0.127) sits just above the real range. Only the tripod legs carry faint wood grain. B: the green barrels are matte rubber against darker satin eyecups and a ribbed centre bar, so gloss varies within the object. Both are soft, so the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Make the telescope tube satin painted metal with a soft broad sheen instead of a wet lacquer streak; keep the gold rings shinier than the tube and the wooden legs fully matte.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is smooth satin-like red with soft folds and no added grain, close to the airbrushed finish of real cards, though it leans towards inflated plastic. B: the meteor rock has an even fine sandy stipple over the whole surface, like the speckle added to generated cards in the lessons, and its flat facets look moulded from clay.
pairs.fix: Remove the uniform fine speckle from the rock; paint it as smooth soft-shaded stone with only a few small chips and pits around the craters.

pairs.difference: A: the dish has hairline panel seams, and the blue base has a riveted plate with evenly spaced hard studs on a lacquered finish, the added crisp hardware seen on generated lesson cards. Its 0.195 highlight share is near the top of the real range. B: the sand towers are soft and matte with granular beach sand, and the scratched brick marks stay quiet.
pairs.fix: Drop the bolted plate and most of the rivets; make the base soft satin paint with a few broad panel lines, and remove the hairline seams from the dish.

pairs.difference: Both exceed the real range for detail, micro texture and gloss, but A exceeds it further. A: the rover has sharp panel gaps, screwed plates, solar cell lines and hard enamel highlights on nearly every part, including the white roof and orange body. B: the taxi's yellow body is softer and more uniform, with blurred window reflections and a quieter finish.
pairs.fix: Remove the screws and thin panel gaps; soften the edges and make the orange body semi-matte, with shine kept to the windshield and headlights.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers mix dotted matte mesh, satin overlays, cord laces and a smoother sole. This range of finishes is broad, but its gloss (0.267) and detail are at the top of the real range. B: the helmet is a single smooth ceramic shell around a wet mirror visor with a hard hot highlight, with thin engraved seams and no intermediate finish.
pairs.fix: Give the helmet shell a soft matte painted finish with slight wear-free tonal variation, and calm the visor highlight into a broader, softer reflection.

pairs.difference: A: the inflatable rings and duck are soft vinyl with quiet sheen and smoothed water, though low in detail (0.0175) and gloss (0.028), and the fence grain is rather large. B: the jacket reads as moulded foam or clay with a fine even surface grain. There is no cloth weave or real stitching, and the pockets look pressed in, while the badges are hard enamel.
pairs.fix: Make the jacket read as soft cotton cloth: thin folds, small neat stitch lines at pocket edges and cuffs, and no foam-like puffiness or surface speckle.

pairs.difference: A: the bar front has visible concrete speckle, the thatch is chunky decorative slats, and the wall has heavy wood marks, giving busy texture across many materials. B: the dome has clean soft glass with broad highlights over smooth matte plaster and little added texture, which is closer to real softness. Measurements are nearly equal, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Remove the concrete speckle from the bar and smooth it to soft painted plaster; shrink the wood and thatch marks so they stay fine and quiet.

pairs.difference: A: the planet is an airbrushed waxy ball with gloss 0.0, below the real range, and has no surface character beyond tiny craters. Only the ring looks shiny. B: the sandals have a matte foam sole with small raised dots against a shinier streaked strap, a believable matte-and-shiny mix with gloss in range.
pairs.fix: Give the planet a soft sheen on its lit side and subtle tonal variation along the bands, so it reads as a solid surface rather than wax.

pairs.difference: A: the table has streaky saturated orange grain, large enough to look decorative like the bold desks in the generated lessons, and the paper is broad bright white with highlight share 0.453, far above the real range. B: the chair has thin matte canvas with a plain seam and dull satin metal tubes, quiet though slightly mottled.
pairs.fix: Make the wood grain fine, low-contrast and quiet, in a calmer tan; shade the paper as warm off-white with a soft falloff rather than a broad blown-out white.

pairs.difference: A: the player is soft-touch orange rubber with fine grooves, and the earbuds are smooth satin white, with restrained highlights. B: the saucer has large drawn horizontal brushed-metal streaks wrapped around the hull, a decorative texture at too big a scale. The lacquered green dome and glowing beads add more wet shine.
pairs.fix: Replace the brushed streaks with smooth soft-shaded silver metal with one broad highlight band; make the dome less wet and the lights simple small painted beads.

pairs.difference: A: the popcorn is lumpy and matte, the cart paint is satin, and the glass is thin and clear, with detail and gloss inside the real range. B: the panel has crisp metal rims and every button, gauge bezel and body surface is the same polished plastic with hard edge highlights, plus a mirror-like floor reflection. Detail (0.058), micro texture (0.024) and gloss (0.149) all exceed the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the teal body satin painted metal, the buttons soft matte plastic and the gauge rims quiet grey; remove the floor reflection and keep only one or two small highlights.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket has satin silver with small rivets, glassy portholes and lacquered red fins. B: the submarine has lacquered yellow with small rivets and copper rims. Both have believable metal and glass, comparable shine and in-range numbers, so finish gives no reason to choose.

pattern: Generated cards tend to give themselves away with an even hard-surface finish: one lacquer or enamel across most parts. They also add crisp hardware such as rivets, screwed plates and hairline seams, plus uniform fine speckle on rock and concrete, and decorative oversized texture such as streaky wood and brushed-metal lines. Real cards stay softer, with quieter grain and a more varied matte-to-satin range. Most calls here are weak (confidence 2–3); p11 is the clearest case.
